## Purpose

This procedure describes the proper use, sample storage protocols, and
inventory management for the laboratory refrigerator (4 C), freezer
(approximately --30 C), and ultra-low freezer (approximately --80 C).
Proper cold storage is essential for preserving sample integrity for
chemical, biological, and molecular analyses [@apha2012].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the laboratory refrigerator (4 C), freezer
  (--30 C), and ultra-low freezer (--80 C) for sample preservation and
  reagent storage
- **Does not apply to:** Food storage (prohibited), field coolers, or
  cryogenic storage (liquid nitrogen)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Definitions

- **Cold chain:** The unbroken sequence of refrigerated storage and
  transport that maintains samples at the required temperature from
  collection through analysis; a break in the cold chain may compromise
  sample integrity.
- **Cryogenic storage:** Storage at temperatures below -80 °C, achieved
  with ultra-low freezers or liquid nitrogen dewars; required for DNA,
  RNA, enzymes, and some biological samples.
- **Freezer burn:** Dehydration and oxidation of samples stored
  improperly in a freezer, caused by sublimation of ice crystals;
  prevented by airtight sealing of containers.
- **Holding temperature:** The target storage temperature specified by
  the analytical method or regulatory protocol for a given sample type
  (e.g., 4 °C for water samples, -20 °C for soil extracts, -80 °C for
  nucleic acids).
- **Temperature excursion:** An event in which the storage temperature
  falls outside the acceptable range; must be documented and the
  potential impact on sample integrity evaluated.
- **Ultra-low freezer (-80 °C):** A mechanical freezer capable of
  maintaining temperatures between -70 °C and -86 °C; used for long-
  term storage of DNA, RNA, microbial cultures, and enzyme preparations.

## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve storage assignments, ensure training compliance |
| Lab Manager       | Monitor temperatures, coordinate power outage response |
| Trained Personnel | Store and retrieve samples following this SOP, maintain inventory records |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |

## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** The --80 C freezer poses a risk of cold burns
  (frostbite) upon contact with surfaces or samples. Heavy drawers and
  racks can cause crush injuries if dropped.
- **Chemical:** No flammable materials may be stored in the laboratory
  refrigerator or freezers. These units are not explosion-proof and can
  generate significant static electricity, which can cause an explosion
  in the presence of flammable fumes.
- **Electrical:** Power outages can compromise stored samples (see
  Section 7).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
No food or beverages shall be stored in the laboratory refrigerator or
freezers under any circumstances.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Insulated cryogenic mittens or gloves (required for --80 C freezer)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Safety glasses (when handling chemical reagents from cold storage)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For cold burns, warm the affected area gradually with lukewarm water; do
not rub. Seek medical attention if blistering occurs. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).

## Procedure

### Refrigerator (4 C)

1. Store samples that require short-term cold storage (soil extracts,
   water samples awaiting analysis, reagents with refrigeration
   requirements)
2. Label all containers with: sample ID, date, researcher name, and
   project
3. Do not overcrowd the refrigerator; allow air circulation around
   samples
4. Remove expired samples and reagents during monthly cleanouts
5. *TBD -- define shelf assignment system for the refrigerator*

### Freezer (--30 C)

1. Store samples requiring medium-term frozen storage (archived soil
   samples, tissue samples, reagents requiring --20 C or colder)
2. Label all containers with: sample ID, date, researcher name, and
   project
3. Organize samples by project; do not mix projects within the same
   shelf area
4. *TBD -- define shelf assignment and inventory system for the --30 C
   freezer*

### Ultra-Low Freezer (--80 C)

The --80 C freezer is organized using a hierarchical location system.
Every sample must be documented in the
[Freezer Inventory Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ohQFRFMBHCu2Wm8H58UH67SJ_uvwSsbRFGZVjZr9Bjc/edit?usp=sharing)
and in your laboratory notebook.

#### Loading Protocol

1. When loading the freezer for the first time or after defrosting,
   install a few drawers at a time from top to bottom, allowing the
   freezer to stabilize between additions
2. Only open the freezer when you are ready to place or remove samples.
   Minimize the time the door is open.
3. Wear insulated cryogenic mittens and a lab coat when accessing the
   freezer

#### Location Hierarchy

The freezer inventory uses the following hierarchy:

- **Shelf:** Each shelf is contained behind an inner door, numbered from
  top to bottom. (Note: Shelf 1 is currently empty.)
- **Divider:** Each divider is a column of drawers within the shelf,
  labeled A through E from left to right
- **Drawer:** Drawers are numbered sequentially from top to bottom
  within each divider
- **Box:** Each drawer contains five boxes, labeled 1 through 5 from
  front to back
- **Box position:** Each box is divided into 100 positions. Numbering
  runs from front-left (position 1) to back-right (position 100),
  counting along rows from left to right

#### Required Inventory Fields

Record the following in the
[Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ohQFRFMBHCu2Wm8H58UH67SJ_uvwSsbRFGZVjZr9Bjc/edit?usp=sharing)
and in your lab notebook each time you store or remove a sample:

| Field              | Description                              |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Shelf              | Shelf number (top to bottom)             |
| Divider            | Column letter (A--E, left to right)      |
| Drawer             | Drawer number (top to bottom)            |
| Box                | Box number (1--5, front to back)         |
| Box position       | Position number (1--100)                 |
| Project            | Project name or code                     |
| Date collected     | Date sample was collected in the field   |
| Sample ID          | Unique sample identifier                 |
| Sample description | Description including any relevant analytical results (e.g., NanoDrop concentration) |

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Before opening the freezer, identify the exact shelf, divider, drawer,
box, and position you need. Have all your samples labeled and ready to
go. This minimizes the time the door is open and protects the integrity
of all stored samples.
:::


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Temperature Monitoring

- Check and record the temperature of each unit daily (or use a
  continuous temperature logger)
- Acceptable ranges: refrigerator 2--6 C; freezer --25 to --35 C;
  ultra-low freezer --75 to --85 C
- If temperature is outside the acceptable range, investigate
  immediately (door left ajar, power outage, compressor failure)
- *TBD -- establish an alarm system or temperature logging protocol
  with automatic notifications*

### Power Outage Protocol

::: {.callout-important}
### Power Outage Response

If the power goes out, it is imperative that valuable samples in either
freezer be moved to a location where power is currently available to
maintain freezing conditions. The laboratory generators do not provide
sufficient power to keep any of the refrigerators or freezers at their
appropriate temperatures.

1. Contact the lab manager and PI immediately
2. Do not open freezer doors unless moving samples to a backup location
3. A closed --80 C freezer can maintain temperature for approximately
   24 hours if the door remains shut
4. If power is not expected to be restored within 4 hours, arrange to
   transfer critical samples to a backup freezer on campus
5. *TBD -- identify backup freezer locations on campus and establish
   agreements for emergency sample transfer*
:::

### Inventory Maintenance

- Conduct a full inventory audit of the --80 C freezer at least once
  per semester
- Remove samples from completed or abandoned projects promptly
- Ensure the Google Sheet is current; discrepancies between the sheet
  and actual contents must be resolved immediately


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                  | Disposal Method                          |
|:----------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Expired or abandoned samples | Dispose per the relevant SOP for the sample type (e.g., biohazard, chemical waste, standard trash) |
| Broken cryovials            | Sweep up carefully; treat as sharps if broken glass |
| Used cryoboxes              | Standard trash (if uncontaminated)       |

## Training Record

Before using the laboratory cold storage independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate proper use of cryogenic PPE
3. Demonstrate the ability to locate a sample using the freezer
   hierarchy and Google Sheet
4. Successfully store and retrieve a sample under supervision, updating
   the inventory in both the Google Sheet and lab notebook
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
